answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock scarce tokens in a public vault and earn access to valuable tasks only after completing work that peers verify. A mirror check compares its signed work history across independent markets, making copied identities or reused credentials easier to flag. Sybils can still appear, but each one ties up capital and must build a separate record; an attacker pays those deposits and verification costs for every identity, while risking slashing for provable fraud. At a summit, participants can raise the bond or tighten review when attacks surge.
